dedupe_keys.name: scout us building sector energy emissions and cost model

description: Scout is an open-source model that estimates the effects of energy conservation measures in US residential and commercial buildings: energy savings, avoided carbon dioxide, operating cost reductions and cost-effectiveness under several technology adoption scenarios, for the whole country and by climate zone, building class and end use. It is developed by the US national laboratories for the Department of Energy's Building Technologies Office, with Jared Langevin of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and Chioke Harris of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory among its authors. Two Zenodo datasets carry its outputs: benchmark scenarios for building energy and CO2 to 2050 (version 6.1, 13 February 2024), with results, measure sets and a scenario guide; and hourly baselines of building electricity use, cost and emissions for 2018 and 2030 (4 October 2019), which apportion Annual Energy Outlook totals across the hours of the year. Coverage: the US building sector. Access: command-line source on GitHub (latest tag v1.2.3), online documentation and a web app with a baseline energy calculator. Licence: Apache 2.0, with a BSD alternative for qualifying contributors; datasets CC BY 4.0. Free. Caveats: the README warns contents are in progress and not error-free. Simulation uses: national building decarbonisation and demand flexibility scenarios. Related records: the grid-interactive efficient building technology data and the EIA RECS and CBECS surveys.
